prompt: ser or estar: Yo ___ de Texas. (I'm from Texas)
explanation: ser for origin and identity: soy de Texas, soy estadounidense. estar never marks where you are from.

prompt: ser or estar: Mi hermana ___ enfermera. (My sister is a nurse)
explanation: ser for professions and roles, usually with no article: es enfermera, es maestro, soy veterano.

prompt: ser or estar: ¿Dónde ___ el baño? (Where is the bathroom?)
explanation: estar for the location of people and things: ¿dónde está? Only events use ser for location (la fiesta es en mi casa).

prompt: ser or estar: ___ las tres de la tarde. (It's three in the afternoon)
explanation: ser for clock time, dates and days: son las tres, es la una, es lunes, es 5 de mayo.

prompt: ser or estar: Hoy ___ muy cansado. (Today I'm very tired)
explanation: estar for temporary states and feelings: estoy cansado, estoy feliz, estoy enojado, estoy crudo.

prompt: ser or estar: Mi abuelo ___ muerto. (My grandfather is dead)
explanation: Death is treated as a resulting state: está muerto, está vivo. A classic trap for English speakers who expect ser.

prompt: ser or estar: La película ___ aburrida. (The movie is boring)
explanation: ser aburrido = boring (a trait of the thing). estar aburrido = bored (how someone feels right now).

prompt: ser or estar: Los niños ___ aburridos, no hay nada que hacer. (The kids are bored)
explanation: estar aburrido = bored, a current feeling. 'Son aburridos' would mean they are boring people.

prompt: ser or estar: Mi hija ___ muy lista; siempre saca diez. (My daughter is very smart)
explanation: ser listo = clever, smart (a trait). estar listo = ready (a state). 'Sacar diez' = get a perfect grade.

prompt: ser or estar: ¿Ya ___ listos para salir? (Are you all ready to leave?)
explanation: estar listo = ready. '¿Ya están listos?' is the normal question before leaving. ustedes takes the same form as ellos.

prompt: ser or estar: Ahorita ___ comiendo, te llamo luego. (I'm eating right now, I'll call you later)
explanation: estar + gerund for actions in progress: estoy comiendo, está trabajando. Never ser. 'Ahorita' = right now (Mexico).

prompt: ser or estar: La reunión ___ en la oficina de Marta. (The meeting is in Marta's office)
explanation: Events (fiesta, reunión, concierto, boda) take ser for where they happen. Objects and people take estar.

prompt: ser or estar: Esta sopa ___ muy rica. (This soup is really good)
explanation: estar for how food tastes right now: está rica, está salado. ser describes the dish in general (el ceviche es rico).

prompt: ser or estar: Carlos ___ casado y tiene dos hijos. (Carlos is married)
explanation: Both occur: 'es casado' (civil status) and 'está casado' (state). In Mexico 'está casado' is very common; both are correct.

prompt: ser or estar: Esta mesa ___ de madera. (This table is made of wood)
explanation: ser de + material, owner or origin: es de madera, es de mi mamá, es de Oaxaca.

prompt: el or la: ___ problema (the problem)
explanation: Greek-origin nouns in -ma are masculine: el problema, el sistema, el programa, el clima, el idioma, el tema.

prompt: el or la: ___ mano (the hand)
explanation: la mano is feminine despite ending in -o. Also la foto, la moto, la radio (shortened words).

prompt: el or la: ___ día (the day)
explanation: Memorize these masculine -a nouns: el día, el mapa, el sofá, el planeta. Buenos días, not buenas.

prompt: el or la: ___ agua fría (the cold water)
en: the (f. noun, el before stressed a-)
explanation: Feminine nouns starting with stressed a- take el in the singular: el agua, el alma, el hambre. Plural las aguas; adjectives stay feminine (fría).

prompt: Plural: la ciudad → ___ (the cities)
explanation: Nouns ending in a consonant add -es: ciudad → ciudades, mes → meses, mujer → mujeres. Vowel endings just add -s.

prompt: Plural: el lápiz → ___ (the pencils)
explanation: Final -z becomes -ces in the plural: lápiz → lápices, vez → veces, luz → luces, pez → peces.

prompt: un or una: ___ casa (a house)
explanation: Indefinite articles match gender: un carro, una casa. Plural unos/unas = some, a few.

prompt: Contraction: Voy ___ mercado. (I'm going to the market)
explanation: a + el always contracts to al. a + la stays separate: voy a la tienda. No contraction with él (the pronoun).

prompt: Contraction: Es la casa ___ vecino. (It's the neighbor's house)
explanation: de + el contracts to del. de + la does not: la casa de la vecina. Possession uses de, there is no 's.

prompt: el or la: ___ gente está contenta. (The people are happy)
explanation: la gente is feminine and singular, with a singular verb: la gente está, not están. Same with la familia, la policía.

prompt: Plural: el examen → ___ (the exams)
explanation: Plural adds -es and often a written accent to keep the stress: examen → exámenes, joven → jóvenes, imagen → imágenes.

prompt: el or la: ___ canción (the song)
explanation: Nouns in -ción, -sión, -dad, -tad, -umbre are feminine: la canción, la ciudad, la libertad, la costumbre.

prompt: por or para: Este regalo es ___ ti. (This gift is for you)
explanation: para for the recipient or destination: para ti, para mi mamá, para la oficina, el camión para Puebla.

prompt: por or para: Gracias ___ todo. (Thanks for everything)
explanation: gracias por is fixed: por marks the reason or cause behind something. Gracias por venir, gracias por la ayuda.

prompt: por or para: Estudio ___ ser enfermero. (I'm studying to be a nurse)
explanation: para + infinitive = in order to, the goal: estudio para ser, ahorro para comprar, vine para ayudar.

prompt: por or para: Trabajo ___ la mañana. (I work in the morning)
explanation: por la mañana / por la tarde / por la noche for parts of the day. Mexicans also say 'en la mañana'.

prompt: por or para: Necesito el reporte ___ el lunes. (I need the report by Monday)
explanation: para for deadlines: para el lunes, para mañana, para las cinco. 'Por el lunes' would mean 'around Monday'.

prompt: por or para: Pagué veinte dólares ___ el taxi. (I paid twenty dollars for the taxi)
explanation: por for exchange, price and payment: pagué 20 por el taxi, cambié pesos por dólares, te lo cambio por el tuyo.

prompt: por or para: Caminamos ___ el parque. (We walked through the park)
explanation: por for movement through or along a place: por el parque, por la calle, pasar por tu casa. para marks the destination.

prompt: por or para: Viví en Bogotá ___ dos años. (I lived in Bogotá for two years)
explanation: por for duration: por dos años, por un rato. Many speakers simply drop it: viví dos años en Bogotá.

prompt: por or para: ___ mí, los tacos al pastor son los mejores. (For me, tacos al pastor are the best)
explanation: para mí = for me / in my opinion. por mí = as far as I'm concerned (por mí, está bien). Note mí with accent after a preposition.

prompt: por or para: Llegamos tarde ___ el tráfico. (We arrived late because of the traffic)
explanation: por for the cause: por el tráfico, por la lluvia, por eso (that's why). para never means 'because of'.

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: Ayer ___ al mercado. (Yesterday I went to the market) [ir, yo]
explanation: Preterite for a completed, one-time action with a specific time: ayer fui. ir and ser share the form fui.

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: Cuando ___ niño, vivía en Houston. (When I was a kid, I lived in Houston) [ser, yo]
explanation: Imperfect era for 'when I was a child': an ongoing background period, not an event. 'Cuando era niño' is a fixed frame.

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: Antes ___ mucho café, ahora ya no. (I used to drink a lot of coffee, not anymore) [tomar, yo]
explanation: Imperfect for past habits (used to): tomaba, iba, comía. 'Antes' and 'ya no' signal a habit that ended.

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: ___ las diez cuando llegó el Uber. (It was ten when the Uber arrived) [ser]
explanation: Clock time in the past is always imperfect: eran las diez, era la una. The arrival (llegó) is the preterite event.

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: ___ mucha gente en la fiesta. (There were a lot of people at the party) [haber]
explanation: había describes the scene (background). hubo = something occurred as an event: hubo un accidente, hubo un temblor.

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: Mi mamá ___ cuarenta años cuando nací. (My mom was forty when I was born) [tener]
explanation: Age in the past takes the imperfect: tenía cuarenta años. nací is preterite because birth is the event.

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: ___ a llamarte, pero se me acabó la batería. (I was going to call you, but my battery died) [ir, yo]
explanation: iba a + infinitive = was going to (a plan that didn't happen). Extremely common in excuses: iba a ir, iba a decirte.

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: Estaba cocinando cuando ___ mi hermano. (I was cooking when my brother called) [llamar]
explanation: An ongoing action (estaba cocinando, imperfect) interrupted by a completed one (llamó, preterite). Classic pairing.

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: Anoche no ___ bien. (Last night I didn't sleep well) [dormir, yo]
explanation: Preterite for a finished event in a closed period: anoche, ayer, la semana pasada. dormir: dormí, durmió (o→u in 3rd person).

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: Ella ___ muy cansada después del vuelo. (She was very tired after the flight) [estar]
explanation: estaba paints the state as background. estuvo frames the tiredness as a finished episode. Both are heard; estaba is the default.

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: ___ a mi esposa en una boda en 2015. (I met my wife at a wedding in 2015) [conocer, yo]
explanation: Preterite conocí = met for the first time. Imperfect conocía = already knew. Same shift: supe (found out) vs sabía (knew).

prompt: Preterite or imperfect: Todos los domingos ___ a la casa de mi abuela. (Every Sunday we went to my grandma's house) [ir, nosotros]
explanation: 'Todos los domingos', 'siempre', 'de niño' signal a habit: imperfect íbamos. ir imperfect: iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, iban.

prompt: Replace the object with a pronoun: Compré el pan. → ___ compré. (I bought it)
explanation: Direct object pronouns: lo/la (it, him/her), los/las (them). They go right before the conjugated verb.

prompt: Replace the object with a pronoun: Vi a María ayer. → ___ vi ayer. (I saw her yesterday)
explanation: la = her / it (f.). The personal 'a' disappears when the noun is replaced: vi a María → la vi.

prompt: Replace both objects: Le di el regalo a mi hermana. → ___ di. (I gave it to her)
explanation: le + lo becomes se lo: two l- pronouns can't stand together. Order is always indirect (se) then direct (lo).

prompt: Fill: ¿Me pasas la sal? → Sí, ___ paso. (Yes, I'll pass it to you)
explanation: Indirect (te) before direct (la): te la paso. Both pronouns go before the conjugated verb.

prompt: Attach the pronoun: Voy a comprar el boleto. → Voy a ___. (I'm going to buy it)
explanation: With an infinitive you can attach the pronoun (comprarlo) or put it before the conjugated verb (lo voy a comprar). Both correct.

prompt: Replace the object: Estoy buscando las llaves. → ___ (I'm looking for them)
explanation: With a gerund: before the auxiliary (las estoy buscando) or attached with a written accent (estoy buscándolas).

prompt: Command with pronouns: Dame el teléfono. → ___ (Give it to me)
explanation: Affirmative commands attach the pronouns: dámelo (da + me + lo). The written accent keeps the stress on dá.

prompt: Make it negative: Dámelo. → No ___. (Don't give it to me)
explanation: Negative commands put the pronouns before the verb, and the verb takes the subjunctive form: no me lo des, no se lo digas.

prompt: gustar: ___ la música cumbia. (I like cumbia music)
explanation: gustar agrees with the thing liked, not with the person: me gusta la música (sing.), me gustan los tacos (pl.).

prompt: gustar: ___ los tacos de canasta. (I like basket tacos)
explanation: Plural thing liked → gustan. encantar, interesar, molestar, faltar, doler all work the same way: me duelen los pies.

prompt: Fill for emphasis: ___ me gusta el café sin azúcar. (Me, I like coffee without sugar)
explanation: a mí / a ti / a él / a ella / a nosotros add emphasis or contrast with gustar. mí (pronoun) always carries an accent; mi (my) does not.

prompt: Fill: ___ dije la verdad a mis papás. (I told my parents the truth)
explanation: les = to them / to you all (indirect object). Spanish keeps les even when 'a mis papás' is also stated: redundant but required.

prompt: Reflexive: ___ llamo Lloyd. (My name is Lloyd)
explanation: llamarse = to be called. me llamo, te llamas, se llama, nos llamamos, se llaman. ¿Cómo te llamas? / ¿Cómo se llama? (usted)

prompt: Reflexive: Ella ___ fue sin despedirse. (She left without saying goodbye)
explanation: irse (to leave) is reflexive: se fue = she left. fue alone = went (ir) or was (ser). ¡Ya me voy! = I'm leaving.

prompt: Reflexive: ___ vemos mañana. (See you tomorrow)
explanation: nos vemos = see you (we see each other), reciprocal use. Also nos hablamos, nos escribimos, nos conocemos.

prompt: Reflexive: ¿A qué hora ___ levantas? (What time do you get up?)
explanation: Reflexive pronouns: me, te, se, nos, se. Daily routine verbs: levantarse, bañarse, vestirse, acostarse.

prompt: Reflexive: Mis hijos ___ acuestan a las nueve. (My kids go to bed at nine)
explanation: se serves él/ella/usted and ellos/ellas/ustedes. acostarse is stem-changing: se acuestan (o→ue), nos acostamos.

prompt: Reflexive with infinitive: Tengo que ___ temprano. (I have to get up early) [levantarse]
explanation: With an infinitive the reflexive pronoun matches the subject and attaches: tengo que levantarme, tienes que levantarte. 'Me tengo que levantar' also fine.

prompt: Write the question with correct punctuation: tienes hambre (are you hungry?)
explanation: Spanish uses an inverted ¿ at the start and ? at the end. No word-order change is needed; intonation does the work.

prompt: qué or que: ¿___ quieres comer? (What do you want to eat?)
explanation: qué with an accent = what / which (question or exclamation). que without accent = that / which (connector).

prompt: qué or que: Dice ___ llega tarde. (He says he's arriving late)
explanation: que without an accent is the conjunction 'that'. The accent appears only in direct and indirect questions (no sé qué quiere).

prompt: cómo or como: ¿___ se dice 'bathroom' en español? (How do you say 'bathroom' in Spanish?)
explanation: cómo = how (question). como = like / as, or 'I eat'. ¿Cómo se dice...? is your best friend as a learner.

prompt: dónde or donde: Esta es la casa ___ nací. (This is the house where I was born)
explanation: donde without accent joins clauses (the house where...). ¿Dónde? with accent asks a question, even indirectly: no sé dónde está.

prompt: Negation: Hay algo en la caja. → No hay ___ en la caja. (There's nothing in the box)
explanation: Spanish doubles negatives: no... nada, no... nadie, no... nunca. 'No hay nada' is correct, not a mistake.

prompt: Negation: ___ conozco a nadie aquí. (I don't know anyone here)
explanation: If nadie / nada / nunca come after the verb, 'no' is required before it. Before the verb they stand alone: Nadie me conoce.

prompt: Negation: ___ he estado en Perú. (I have never been to Peru)
explanation: nunca before the verb needs no 'no'. After the verb it does: No he estado nunca en Perú. jamás is a stronger 'never'.

prompt: Tag question: Vives en Guadalajara, ¿___? (You live in Guadalajara, right?)
explanation: ¿verdad? and ¿no? turn a statement into a yes/no check. Also ¿cierto? (Colombia) and the casual ¿o no? / ¿o qué?

prompt: Question word: ¿___ cuesta el kilo de tortillas? (How much does a kilo of tortillas cost?)
explanation: cuánto agrees when it modifies a noun: ¿cuántos años? ¿cuántas personas? Always accented in questions. Casual: ¿a cómo el kilo?

prompt: Subjunctive: Quiero que ___ conmigo. (I want you to come with me) [venir, tú]
explanation: quiero que + subjunctive when the wish is about someone else. Same subject takes the infinitive: quiero venir.

prompt: Subjunctive: Ojalá no ___ mañana. (Hopefully it won't rain tomorrow) [llover]
explanation: ojalá (que) always takes the subjunctive: ojalá llueva, ojalá puedas venir. From Arabic 'God willing'.

prompt: Subjunctive: Es importante que ___ agua. (It's important that you drink water) [tomar, tú]
explanation: Impersonal es + adjective + que (importante, necesario, mejor, raro) triggers the subjunctive: es mejor que te vayas.

prompt: Subjunctive: Cuando ___ a casa, te llamo. (When I get home, I'll call you) [llegar, yo]
explanation: cuando + a future event takes the subjunctive: cuando llegue. A habit takes the indicative: cuando llego, siempre ceno. Note g→gu.

prompt: Subjunctive: Te lo explico para que lo ___. (I'll explain it so that you understand) [entender, tú]
explanation: para que always takes the subjunctive. Stem change is kept: entender → entiendas, poder → puedas.

prompt: Subjunctive: Espero que todo ___ bien. (I hope everything goes well) [salir]
explanation: espero que + subjunctive. Subjunctive builds on the irregular yo stem: salgo → salga, tengo → tenga, digo → diga.

prompt: Subjunctive: No creo que ___ tiempo hoy. (I don't think there's time today) [haber]
explanation: no creo que expresses doubt and takes the subjunctive. Plain creo que takes the indicative: creo que hay tiempo.

prompt: Subjunctive: Que ___ buen viaje. (Have a good trip) [tener, tú]
explanation: Wishes with bare 'que' use the subjunctive with 'espero' implied: que tengas buen viaje, que te vaya bien, que descanses.

prompt: tú command: ___ más despacio, por favor. (Speak more slowly, please) [hablar]
explanation: The affirmative tú command is the él/ella present form: habla, come, escribe, espera.

prompt: Negative tú command: No ___ tan rápido. (Don't speak so fast) [hablar]
explanation: Negative tú commands use the subjunctive form: no hables, no comas, no escribas, no te vayas.

prompt: usted command: ___ aquí, por favor. (Sign here, please) [firmar]
explanation: usted commands use the subjunctive form, affirmative and negative: firme, no firme; pase, espere, disculpe. Standard at banks and offices.

prompt: Irregular tú command: ___ acá. (Come here) [venir]
explanation: Irregular tú commands: ven, pon, sal, haz, di, ve, ten, sé. 'Ven acá' and 'ven para acá' are very common in Mexico.

prompt: Irregular tú command: ___ la tarea antes de salir. (Do your homework before going out) [hacer]
explanation: haz (hacer), pon (poner), di (decir), sal (salir), ten (tener), ve (ir), sé (ser), ven (venir). 'Hazlo' = do it.

tl: La fiesta {{es}} en casa de Luis.
en: The party is at Luis's house.
Are you ready yet? The Uber is here.

tl: Buenas tardes, ¿{{está}} la doctora Ruiz, por favor?
en: Good afternoon, is Dr. Ruiz in, please?
hint: ser or estar, present, ella (formal phone call)
ser or estar, present, ellos (taste right now)

tl: {{El}} problema es que no tengo efectivo.
en: The problem is I don't have cash.
I bought some flowers for my mother-in-law.
There are a lot of young people in the plaza.
This coffee is for you, ma'am.
I go running in the morning.
hint: por or para (part of the day)

en: I need the visa by Friday.

tl: Cambié dólares {{por}} pesos en la casa de cambio.
en: I exchanged dollars for pesos at the exchange place.
I'm saving up to buy a motorcycle.

tl: Pasamos {{por}} tu casa a las siete.
en: We'll stop by your house at seven.
Yesterday I went to the market.

tl: Cuando {{era}} niño, jugaba fútbol todos los días.
en: When I was a kid, I played soccer every day.

tl: Anoche {{cenamos}} en un puesto de la esquina.
en: Last night we had dinner at a corner food stand.
There was a lot of traffic on the Periférico.

tl: Mi abuela siempre {{hacía}} tamales en diciembre.
en: My grandma always made tamales in December.

tl: {{Iba}} a escribirte, pero se me olvidó.
en: I was going to text you, but I forgot.

tl: {{Eran}} las once cuando por fin llegó el camión.
en: It was eleven when the bus finally came.

tl: El año pasado {{viajé}} a Colombia con mi esposa.
en: Last year I traveled to Colombia with my wife.

tl: Estábamos viendo la tele cuando {{se fue}} la luz.
en: We were watching TV when the power went out.

tl: Mi tío {{tenía}} treinta años cuando llegó a Estados Unidos.
en: My uncle was thirty when he came to the US.
The bread? I bought it at the bakery.

tl: A mi mamá {{la}} llamo todos los domingos.
en: I call my mom every Sunday.

tl: ¿Las fotos? Ya {{se las}} mandé a Pedro.
en: The photos? I already sent them to Pedro.
Can I borrow your charger? —Sure, I'll lend it to you.

hint: dar, tú command + me + lo (one word)

tl: No {{me lo}} digas, ya lo sé.
en: Don't tell me, I already know.

tl: A ella no {{le}} gusta el picante.
{{Les}} mandé un mensaje a mis hermanos.
en: I sent my brothers a message.
I'm going to call you later.
hint: llamar + object pronoun attached to infinitive

en: My name is Lloyd, nice to meet you.
Okay, see you then, take care.

tl: Mi vecino {{se fue}} a vivir a Monterrey.

en: What time do you get up on weekdays?
Have a seat, please. What's your name?

hint: question word with accent (casual Mexican greeting)

tl: Disculpe, ¿{{dónde}} queda la parada del camión?
en: Excuse me, where is the bus stop?
How much is a kilo of avocados?
I have nothing to do today.

tl: No conozco a {{nadie}} en esta ciudad.
en: I don't know anyone in this city.
I want you to come to the wedding.
Hopefully you can come on Saturday.

tl: Es importante que {{traiga}} su pasaporte, señor.
en: It's important that you bring your passport, sir.
When you arrive, let me know.
Take care / hope it goes well.
